reason: E1 supports the feasibility of laser-clad TiAl coatings on TC4 for wear resistance via solid-solution strengthening, but does not address composite coatings with hard particles. E3 supports the hardening and wear-resistance benefits of WC particles in a metallic matrix, but in the context of HEAs and plasma cladding, not TiAl-based laser cladding on TC4. E2 is about a different material system (AlCoCrFeNiTi HEA with MoS2) and does not support any key premise. The premise of retaining beneficial properties and preventing delamination is not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Laser cladding can produce TiAl-based coatings on TC4 that improve wear resistance via solid-solution strengthening
Dispersed hard ceramic particles (e.g., WC) can be incorporated into a metallic coating to enhance hardness and wear resistance
The hard particles act as barriers to plastic deformation and abrasive wear, and can limit grain growth
A metallurgically bonded coating can be formed that retains substrate toughness and prevents delamination
The coating will not degrade the inherent beneficial properties of TC4 (e.g., lightweight, ductility, corrosion resistance)
